claims.harm: ChaCha20 produced incorrect output on big-endian platforms
claims.quote: My biggest objection currently is that it's broken on big-endian systems - left a suggestion how to reproduce and fix it.

claims.harm: Severe ~2x performance regression compared to scalar on ARM64 when compiled with GCC
claims.quote: RPi5 with GCC shows a regression: the generic vectorized implementation is ~2x slower than scalar on ARM64 with GCC, while Clang handles it fine.
claims.settled_by_quote: The second introduces a pluggable vector interface, and adds a 128bit implementation. This works around gcc's vectorizer's limitations and should fix the performance regressions you pointed out.

claims.harm: Circular include dependency between chacha20_vec and chacha20_vec_128impl breaks CI linting
claims.quote: Note that the CI indicates a dependency-cycle regression was introduced here.

claims.harm: Untested multi-block dispatch states, a ~7% regression on 64-byte inputs, and potential IBD slowdown on some platforms
claims.quote: Corecheck currently has no coverage data for the new code and measures the 64-byte case about 7% slower... To be more confident in the correctness, I would like to see the new path covered by: tests... benchmarks... fuzz target...

support.reason: Approach looks very nice, and at least going by the bench results, gives a good improvement.

result.notes: Initial big-endian failure was resolved by pushing l0rinc's byte-swap fix. The severe GCC ARM64 regression was resolved by switching from a 256-bit to a 128-bit vector approach. l0rinc's latest review requests PR restructuring, coverage of all dispatch branches via unit tests/fuzzing/benchmarks, and addressing CI dependency cycle lint.
